lesson.title: NATO and the Atlantic
lesson.summary: How the world's leading military alliance works and why it still matters in the 21st century.

blocks.text: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) is a military alliance founded in 1949 to ensure the collective defense of its member states. Its central principle: an attack on one member is an attack on all.
Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty is the backbone of the alliance. It has been invoked only once in history — after the September 11, 2001 attacks in the United States.

With Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, NATO returned to the center of geopolitical debate. Historically neutral countries like Finland and Sweden joined the alliance — showing how European security has transformed.
NATO is the most successful defense alliance in history. — Anders Fogh Rasmussen

cards.front: Why did Finland and Sweden join NATO?
cards.back: Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 changed the security calculus of these historically neutral countries.

quiz.question: What is the central principle of NATO's Article 5?
options: Each nation defends only its own territory
An attack on one member is an attack on all
Only nuclear attacks trigger collective defense
quiz.explanation: Article 5 establishes collective defense: an attack against one ally requires a response from all members.

quiz.question: What led Finland and Sweden to abandon neutrality and join NATO?
options: A formal invitation from the European Union
A direct attack on their territories
quiz.explanation: The war in Ukraine demonstrated the risks of neutrality facing an expansionist Russia, leading both countries to seek NATO's protection.
